agent_role: Extension Hijacker — boundary crossing, proxy/diamond, hook trust model

findings.title: validateHandlerOrder overflow bypass allows handler orders to exceed max pricing bounds
confidence_deductions: -10: requires specific token/pool configuration (max-only bounds, no min bound)
-10: requires handler integration (CLOB or Permit handler must be active)
findings.description: In AMMStandardHook.validateHandlerOrder (lines 198-226), when computeRatioX96 returns 0 due to uint160 overflow, neither the min nor max pricing bound check triggers. With max-only bounds (minSqrtPriceX96=0, maxSqrtPriceX96>0), an order with an extreme token ratio (amount1 >> amount0 causing overflow) is accepted despite the effective price far exceeding the configured maximum. The function _validatePricingBounds (line 847-849) correctly checks for sqrtPriceX96==0 and reverts, but validateHandlerOrder lacks this check entirely.
findings.impact: Token creator who sets max-only pricing bounds to prevent their token from trading at extreme prices gets no protection for handler orders. An attacker can fill handler orders at prices above the intended ceiling. Impact depends on the specific token and max bound — could range from negligible to significant price manipulation for tokens that rely on max bounds as their primary price safety mechanism.
findings.proof_sketch: Integration test at lbamm-hooks-and-handlers/test/AuditExtHijackerOverflow.t.sol:test_validateHandlerOrder_overflowBypassesMaxBound confirms that an order with amountOut=type(uint160).max passes validateHandlerOrder despite max bound set at 1e30. The computeRatioX96 returns 0, and 0 > maxBound evaluates to false.
findings.victim: Token creators who rely on max-only pricing bounds for handler orders
findings.extractable_value: Variable — depends on token value and configured max bound. For high-value tokens, could enable significant price ceiling bypass. No direct fund extraction but enables unfavorable fills.
attack_sequence: 1. Identify token with max-only pricing bounds (minSqrtPriceX96=0, maxSqrtPriceX96=X) on AMMStandardHook
2. Create handler order (via CLOB or Permit handler) with amountIn=1 wei and amountOut >= type(uint160).max
4. validateHandlerOrder checks: min != 0 && 0 < min -> false (skip), max != 0 && 0 > max -> false (pass)
5. Order is validated and accepted at an effective price far above the configured maximum
prerequisites: Token must have max-only pricing bounds set (no min bound)
Token must use a transfer handler (CLOB or Permit) that calls validateHandlerOrder
Attacker must be able to submit handler orders

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R2-DP-09: Operator precedence bug in ModuleLiquidity.createPool — deposit0 | deposit1 == 0
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Solidity operator precedence differs from C/C++. In Solidity, | (bitwise OR) has HIGHER precedence than == (position 8 vs 10). Expression deposit0 | deposit1 == 0 correctly evaluates as (deposit0 | deposit1) == 0, which is the intended behavior.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R2-DP-03: Reentrancy during queued hook fee distribution — collectHookFeesByHook lacks nonReentrant modifier
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Structural concern confirmed but below submission threshold. ENTERED bit blocks ALL nonReentrant-protected entry points. Exploitation requires ERC-777 token + hook as fee recipient. Prerequisites too narrow for Medium+ severity.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R2-HR-01: Registry/Hook initialized flag desync — force re-fetch TOCTOU
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Token admin must call setTokenSettings with initialized=false, then change settings without syncing hook. Admin-controlled self-inflicted behavior. No third-party attacker can trigger the desync.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R2-HR-03: Disabled pool bypass via stale cache — checkDisabledPools flag desync
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Cache desync is documented by-design behavior (AMMStandardHook.sol:605-606). Admin must explicitly sync hooks after settings changes.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R2-HR-04: Auto-cache leaves whitelist empty
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Admin setup issue. Auto-cache copies token settings struct but whitelist content must be synced separately. Self-inflicted DoS on admin's own token.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C7: INV-H01 — External calls to hook functions should revert
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: All state-changing hook functions protected by _requireCallerIsAMM(). validateHandlerOrder is view-only (by design). validateRemoveLiquidity/validateCollectFees always revert.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C8: INV-H02 — Settlement conservation: balance snapshots around ammHandleTransfer
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: AMMModule enforces strict balance checking: balanceInBefore captured before transfer, balanceInAfter verified after. If balanceInBefore + amountIn != balanceInAfter, reverts.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C9: INV-H04 — Hook fee integrity: max fee cap and overflow
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Hook fees calculated by _calculateFee using FullMath.mulDiv with MAX_BPS. Fee rate is uint16. _storeTokensOwed has overflow check. No overflow path found.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C10: INV-SW04 — Output bounded by reserves
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Pool types enforce output bounds via liquidity/price curve math. Output cannot exceed reserves. Additionally limitAmount checks enforce user-specified bounds.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C11: INV-S04 — Denomination consistency: fee token matches computation token
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: All fees in _performSettlement (protocol, exchange, feeOnTop) use swapOrder.tokenIn. No denomination mismatch.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C12: INV-E03 — Sandwich resistance via limitAmount
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: AMMModule enforces limitAmount: amountOut < limitAmount reverts (input swap), amountIn > limitAmount reverts (output swap). Victim always gets at least their configured minimum.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C13: Pool ID encoding validation
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: AMMModule validates poolId structure after pool type creates it: PoolDecoder.getPoolType must match, PoolDecoder.getPoolFee must match.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C14: createPool with edge parameters
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Edge parameters validated by pool type implementation. Core only validates poolId consistency and uniqueness.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C15: Storage layout collisions across diamond facets
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: All four diamond modules use Diamond Storage pattern via Storage.appStorage() at base slot 0x9A1D. No slot collision risk.
ruled_out_vectors.test_file: code-analysis: Slither storage layout on all 4 modules shows 0 traditional slots

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C19: Hook/pool accounting desync — Bunni pattern
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: AMMStandardHook is a stateless fee calculator. No internal balance tracking. If afterSwap reverts, entire TX reverts atomically. No Bunni-style desync possible.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C20: Diamond selector collision across all modules
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Checked all 27 functions across 4 diamond facets — 0 selector collisions found.
ruled_out_vectors.test_file: code-analysis: Manual 4-byte selector comparison across all diamond facets

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C21: Transient storage cross-path — ChainSecurity research
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: AMMStandardHook uses exactly ONE transient slot (DIRECT_SWAP_BEFORE_SWAP_AMOUNT_SLOT). Written in beforeSwap, read in afterSwap, both in direct swap path only. No other code path reads this slot.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C22: Hook return value manipulation — Uni V4 vectors
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Hook fee return is bounded by admin-configured BPS rate via _calculateFee. Hook cannot inflate fees beyond configured uint16 BPS. Custom malicious hooks are visible on-chain.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C1: Core->PoolType trust — mock pool type returning inflated amountOut
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: AMMModule verifies balance changes after transfer: balanceInBefore + amountIn must equal balanceInAfter. Fake amounts fail this check.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C2: Core->Handler mismatch — handler expects wrong token pair
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Handler receives tokens as parameters from AMMModule._executeTransferHandler. No stored token pair state to mismatch.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C3: Core->Hook — mock hook returns fee > swap amount
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Hook fee computed from BPS rates (uint16) via _calculateFee. Cannot produce arbitrary fees. AMMModule deducts from swap amount.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C4: Hook->Registry mid-swap settings change
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Settings cached in memory during swap (line 114). Reentrancy guard prevents most reentry. Mid-swap registry changes cannot affect the in-memory copy.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C5: PoolType->Core return — pool returning feeAmount > amountIn
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Pool types don't return fee amounts. Fee computation done by hook + FeeHelper in AMMModule.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C6: Handler->External reentrancy — PermitTransferHandler -> token callback -> reenter AMM
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: ENTERED bit set during swap. All AMM entry points protected by nonReentrant modifier checking ENTERED bit. Token callback cannot reenter.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Target Map H1: Malicious pool type returns fake amounts to steal from LPs
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Balance verification at settlement prevents claiming more tokens than actually moved. Pool type is set at creation and visible on-chain.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Target Map H2: Malicious transfer handler skips actual transfer
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: AMMModule verifies actual balance changes after handler execution (balanceInBefore + amountIn == balanceInAfter). Handler that skips transfer fails this check.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Target Map H3: Malicious hook manipulates price limits
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Pricing bounds set by token admin via registry, not by hook. Hook reads bounds from storage but cannot modify them.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Target Map H4: Pool type address collision via 6 leading zero bytes
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Creating an address with 6 leading zero bytes requires ~2^48 hash operations (computationally infeasible). Pool type registration requires governance.
ruled_out_vectors.test_file: code-analysis: PoolDecoder address extraction + computational infeasibility

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Target Map H5: UUPS/beacon implementation takeover
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Protocol uses Diamond Proxy pattern, not UUPS/beacon. No implementation takeover vector exists.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Target Map H6: Facet selector collision
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: 0 selector collisions found across all 27 functions in 4 diamond facets. Facet management requires governance.
ruled_out_vectors.test_file: code-analysis: Manual 4-byte selector check across all diamond facets

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Target Map H7: CREATE2 -> selfdestruct -> redeploy at trusted address
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: EIP-6780 (Dencun/Cancun) eliminates selfdestruct-redeploy attack. Protocol targets cancun EVM.
ruled_out_vectors.test_file: not-applicable: EIP-6780 eliminates selfdestruct-redeploy on cancun EVM

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Target Map H8: Malicious facet writes to storage slot used by another facet
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: All modules share Diamond Storage via Storage.appStorage(). Adding facets requires governance. No external attacker can add facets.
ruled_out_vectors.test_file: code-analysis: All modules use Storage.appStorage() — shared structured storage

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Target Map H9: Exploit facet management to add malicious facet without governance
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Facet management in secure-proxy requires owner/governance authorization. No public function to add/replace facets.

theft_theses.victim: Token creators who set max-only pricing bounds
theft_theses.asset: Token value via unfavorable trades above intended max price

theft_theses.thesis: Reentrancy through collectHookFeesByHook during queued fee distribution enables double-spend of hook fees
theft_theses.asset: Hook fees denominated in ERC-777 tokens

theft_theses.thesis: Malicious pool type returns inflated amounts to drain LP funds
Malicious transfer handler skips transfer while core credits the swap
Diamond selector collision allows attacker code to intercept admin functions

hypothesis_results.detail: validateHandlerOrder overflow bypass with max-only bounds confirmed. Integration test passes.
Structural concern confirmed but below submission threshold. Requires ERC-777 token + hook as fee recipient.
NOT A BUG. Solidity | has higher precedence than == (position 8 vs 10).
